scope: Original harmonic/transient diagnostic and genuine fixed-state Schafter confirmation

setup.sourceState: Identical deterministic diagnostic PCM at every distance
setup.diagnosticCompensation: Only distance/masterGain applied to sum(L,R)/sqrt(2); compensation never applied to audible output

limitations: Authored coefficients are presentation assumptions, not calibrated atmosphere or a reference-derived physical SPL
Existing complementary first-order 400 Hz and 4 kHz bands overlap; coefficient loss is not a steep physical cutoff or full fogging filter
Linear fractional-delay interpolation introduces baseline high-frequency ripples; compare profiles at the same distance
Source, bearing and orientation are fixed; engine-state changes, physical Doppler, obstruction and room acoustics are deliberately absent
Transient energy/detail metrics do not establish perceptual realism or human listening approval

genuineHeldSource.scope: Genuine held-source distance confirmation; no subjective acceptance claim

source.construction: (calibrated engine + exhaust)/sqrt(2), one co-located diagnostic emitter
source.limitation: Co-location deliberately isolates propagation from separate car emitter positions; not the full spatial vehicle mix

setup.sourceStateProgression: One constant control from startup; internal running/state smoothing only

analysis.compensation: Only analytical distance/master factor on sum(L,R)/sqrt(2); never applied to delivered listening WAVs
analysis.truncation: Each delivered segment is 3 s; far clips end before the last emitted samples arrive. The common emission window ends at 2.1 s, safely before every truncation.

limitations: Authored distance coefficients and geometry are not measured atmospheric or GTA acoustic calibration
Existing first-order 400 Hz/4 kHz complementary bands limit the achievable steepness
Common source/control/geometry isolate distance; absolute native Schafter recognition and mix remain unverified
Simulation startup pose-history exclusions are retained separately from zero renderer PCM-history faults
No new headroom calibration, per-file normalization, gain compensation in delivered WAVs or timing campaign
Temporal modulation and RMS-relative steps characterize signal changes; they do not establish native recognition or perceptual realism
Each spectrum uses the same emitted-time window; no independent level matching or changing operating state is used
